Hi Marissa / Tom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We got a strong thumbs-up from clinical ops — they want to run a 60-day pilot that will hit live patient data (PHI) and needs a clear hosting posture recommendation. Key constraints:
- HIPAA + state-level patient data residency in the US (some records originate in CA).
- SOC 2 Type II evidence and regular access/audit logs.

- Latency target: 150–250ms p95 for interactive workflows.

Emily / Tom — thanks, got the requirements. High level summary below; I'm attaching a short mutual action plan and an initial cost workbook (Draft_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf, Dedicated_vs_Private_costs_v1.xlsx).

TL;DR recommendation: start the pilot on Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in our US region) with a defined escape hatch to Private if policy/procurement needs on-prem isolation. Dedicated hits latency and cost targets faster; Private gives you maximum control and full network isolation but increases lead time and operational overhead.

Why Dedicated for pilot (fastest path):
- Provisioning time: ~2–3 business days for a reserved pool (pilot-sized).
- Footprint we recommend for pilot (sustained 250 concurrent interactive sessions, p95 latency target): 8x H100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool with auto-burst to shared cap.
- Expected performance: p95 latency in 120–260ms depending on prompt token distribution and batching policy.
- Security/compliance: Redwood Dedicated supports SOC 2 evidence, customer-scoped audit logs, and VPC peering options; data residency enforced in us-east1/ us-west1.
- Cost (pilot baseline): ~$125,000/month for the dedicated reserved pool + monitoring/observability add-on. (See workbook for line items and burst pricing.)

Why Private (if procurement requires it):
- Lead time: 3–6 weeks (provisioning, on-prem partner coordination, KMS integration).
- Footprint needed: because of redundancy and on-prem conservative sizing for isolated workloads, we estimate 10–12x H100-equivalent GPUs to match Dedicated's observable throughput and maintain headroom.
- Cost: one-time setup + higher monthly ops (estimated ~$210,000/month equivalent, includes managed ops and 20% allocation for spare capacity).
- Pros: full network control, no shared control plane, easier for strict internal audit policies.

Open items for procurement/ops to confirm:
- Exact region(s) for residency enforcement (we can pin to a single region).
- Desired SLA/uptime targets for pilot vs production.
- Whether Vertex will accept a hybrid approach: Dedicated for pilot, then Private for prod if policy requires.

Next steps I propose:
1) We finalize the mutual action plan and sign it (1–2 business days).
2) Vertex confirms region + SLA target.
3) We provision the Dedicated pilot pool and share runbook + run-of-show for the June pilot start.

Attaching: Draft_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf; Dedicated_vs_Private_costs_v1.xlsx

Subject: Internal — VertexHealth pilot commitment ask + sizing rationale

Team — forwarding Vertex's procurement questions. Putting a proposal on the table we can present to Tom/Emily. Please review and flag any concerns. I included the user requirements and our initial workbook.

Summary of our ask to procurement:
- Pilot: 3-month pilot commitment to qualify for pilot reserved pricing. After pilot, convert to month-to-month or a production annual commit.
- Dedicated footprint recommended for pilot: 8x H100-equivalent GPUs (N=8) in a dedicated pool; burst to shared capacity up to +4 GPUs during peak windows. Rationale: sustained 250 concurrent interactive sessions, avg 200 tokens, batching at 4–8 requests achieves target latency.
- Private footprint if required: 10x H100-equivalent GPUs (N=10) with 2x redundancy nodes for HA, plus on-prem networking and KMS integration (leads to the 10–12 GPU range we gave external).
- Discount ask: recommend offering a 20% discount on list dedicated monthly rate for a 3-month pilot commit. For conversion to Private, credit first-month setup fee up to $50k if they sign annual Private agreement within 90 days of pilot end.

Sizing notes (very rough):
- Token throughput: pilot avg ~50k tokens/min, peak ~120k tokens/min.
- Batch strategy: micro-batching for interactive flows + prefix caching for clinicians reduces token compute by ~18%.
- KV cache and model quantization profile: recommend int8 quantization with preserved fp16 for critical layers; reduces per-token GPU cycles by ~25% in our benchmarks.

Risks / tradeoffs:
- Private setup time and KMS/HSM coordination is the gating item — it frequently adds 2–4 weeks.
- Dedicated pool requires clear routing policy to ensure no noisy neighbor effects; we'll configure strict pool quotas and tracing to prove isolation during pilot.

Decision points for the rep deck: commitment length, discount %, and whether we pre-authorize a $50k setup credit for conversion.

Can we get quick approval on: 20% pilot discount + $50k conversion credit pre-authorization?

Thanks — M

Emily / Tom — circling back with a compact decision brief and an updated MAAP (Vertex_MAAP_v2.docx). Key points below so procurement/legal have what they need: 

1) Pilot path (recommended): Redwood Dedicated — 3-month pilot commit to qualify for the pilot reserved rate. Pricing: $125k/month baseline (post 20% pilot discount already applied in the workbook). Credits: if Vertex converts to Private within 90 days after pilot, Redwood will apply up to $50k credit toward Private setup fees.

2) Lead times: Dedicated provisioning: 2–3 business days after MAAP signature + PO. Private on-prem: 18–35 calendar days depending on KMS/HSM vendor SLAs and on-site networking coordination. We'll provide a dedicated project manager for Private.

3) Technical footprint: Dedicated pilot = 8x H100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool with auto-burst to +4 GPUs; expected p95 latency 120–260ms with micro-batching and prefix caching. Private baseline = 10x H100-equivalent GPUs (2 for HA) to match throughput with additional headroom.

4) SLA & compliance: Redwood Dedicated can scope SOC 2 artifacts and provide customer-scoped audit logs. For highest-evidence audits, Private simplifies some control objectives (full control of network and KMS).

Action items / next steps: 
- Vertex: confirm region (us-east1 or us-west1) and sign MAAP (attached).
- Vertex procurement: issue PO for pilot or confirm auto-billing via credit card.
- Redwood: once MAAP + PO received, we'll provision Dedicated pool, share runbook, and schedule a run-of-show for pilot start (target: 2028-06-21).

If procurement needs a bridged phone call this week to land lead times and credits, happy to jump on a 30-minute call.

Thanks — Marissa
